subject: ISV SDK federation & observability handshake
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Eve Tran <eve.tran@orbitbridge.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: ISV SDK federation & observability handshake

Hi Eve and OrbitBridge SDK team,

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. As discussed, we'd like to propose a lightweight "federation" handshake between Redwood and OrbitBridge so partner apps integrating LangChain/LlamaIndex flows can surface a single correlated trace across: 1) the LangChain runtime call (agent/chain orchestration), 2) token-level generation spans from the model call on Redwood, and 3) document fetch/indexing spans from LlamaIndex.

Attached is a first-pass interop matrix (interop_matrix_v1.xlsx) that attempts to map events and required fields. Key asks from our side:
- Confirm your preferred trace_id/parent_id mapping and any required vendor fields (e.g., orbit_request_id).
- Confirm the minimum telemetry schema (span names, attributes, prompt_hash, model_variant, token_count).
- Agree on an acceptance test: curated prompt set (10 queries) where we can observe full trace stitching in Redwood Console.

We can stand up a two-week sandbox org with a sample LangChain app instrumented by your SDK and our trace-exporter. If that works, we do a joint demo and then a short MSA addendum.

Next steps proposed:
1) You review the interop matrix and push any required fields back to me (or update the sheet).
2) Confirm point-of-contact for telemetry (we'll need one SDK engineer + one product lead).
3) Book a 45-min sync next week for mapping and acceptance criteria.

I've CC'd Vanessa and Priyom who will run the acceptance criteria and test harness respectively. Karthik will own the rollout/rollback policy.

Attachments: interop_matrix_v1.xlsx

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Partner Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0126

--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference runtime

From: Eve Tran <eve.tran@orbitbridge.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: OrbitBridge SDK Team <sdk@orbitbridge.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ISV SDK federation & observability handshake

Thanks Mina — appreciate the clear plan and the matrix. We reviewed the spreadsheet and sketched a minimal telemetry schema (attached) that maps to our current SDK. A few quick notes:

- Trace mapping: we prefer to surface orbit_request_id as a top-level attribute and will emit our own orbit_span_id. We can set orbit_request_id == the LangChain request id if you expose that.
- Prompt attribution: we currently emit prompt_text + prompt_hash; happy to add prompt_digest to match whatever you prefer for deduping.
- Sampling: our SDK defaults to 5% backend sampling but we can expose a flag to force full trace for sandbox runs.

We can commit an SDK engineer (Oliver Grant) for the sync and a product owner (me). Oliver is CC'd from their LangChain liaison and can help map the LangChain runtime spans.

Proposed meeting times (PST): Thu 3/29 10:00 or Fri 3/30 09:00. Which works for your team?

Attaching: orbitbridge_telemetry_schema.json (stub)

--
Eve Tran
Head of Partnerships, OrbitBridge
eve.tran@orbitbridge.ai

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Eve Tran <eve.tran@orbitbridge.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ISV SDK federation & observability handshake

On Wed, Mar 28, 2028 at 8:14 AM Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. As discussed, we'd like to propose a lightweight "federation" handshake...

Eve / OrbitBridge team — this looks good from a commercial/ops standpoint. A few internal notes and acceptance criteria I'm asking the group to confirm before we spin up the sandbox:

Acceptance checklist (summary):
- End-to-end trace stitching: a single trace must show LangChain orchestration -> Redwood model spans -> LlamaIndex document fetch spans.
- Prompt-level attribution: prompt_hash or prompt_digest present on model spans.
- Latency sampling: ability to force-full-sample for the 10 curated prompts.
- Data retention & PII: confirm that prompt_text can be masked in production (we'll only allow full prompt_text in sandbox mode).
- SLO/rollback: define acceptable latency distribution (p50/p95) for the sandbox traffic and a rollback policy if any model variant increases token-cost by > 15% for same quality.

Priyom — please take point on the harness. Action: create a small CI job that runs the 10-prompt set against the integrated sandbox and collects: trace_count, stitched_traces_count, and prompt-attribution-rate. Put the results in the Drive doc linked below.

Karthik — can you prepare a short rollback playbook (2 bullets) for canary failures? We'll attach to the MSA addendum.

If everyone is aligned we'll lock Thu 3/29 10:00 PST for a 45-min mapping session.

Attachments: acceptance_checklist.md

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Director, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Eve Tran <eve.tran@orbitbridge.ai>
